summary: show.mjs's isRefOwnedBySession mirror was NOT extended for the new `human-turn:` namespace, breaking that function's own documented same-commit invariant. `fgos coordination show --json` now reports targetRefOwnedBySession/evidenceRefsOwnedBySession wrongly in BOTH directions for human-turn refs.
evidence: The function's own header comment (show.mjs:22-31) states the rule verbatim: "Every rule the write door gains has to be mirrored here in the same commit, or the two silently disagree about a ref shape only one of them recognizes (MVP8's `contribution:` namespace is one such)." This commit added TWO rules to the write door -- the `human-turn:` prefix ownership branch and the bare-turn-id near-miss refusal (store.mjs:1187-1220) -- and mirrored NEITHER. refOwnedOpts (show.mjs:267) passes contributionIds but no humanTurnIds, and isRefOwnedBySession's destructure (show.mjs:55) has no humanTurnIds parameter at all. Empirically reproduced, both directions: (A) FALSE POSITIVE -- a bare `turn_1` targetRef that the write door refuses outright ('validation': "is the bare id of a human turn this session recorded, which targets nothing") is rendered by show as targetRefOwnedBySession=true, because `turn_1` has no path separator and no `asgn_` segment so it falls through to the unconditional `return true` at show.mjs:78. (B) FALSE NEGATIVE -- a targetRef `human-turn:../victim` that the write door ACCEPTS as owned (the prefix branch at store.mjs:1192 early-returns before the segment scan) is rendered by show as targetRefOwnedBySession=false, because show's mirror never recognizes the prefix and splits the ref into segments, finds `victim`, and sees another session's session.json. Repro: recorded a turn, wrote each disposition, then read showCoordinationUseCase(...).dispositions[0].targetRefOwnedBySession. Also note a third, unproven-but-structural case: ANY `human-turn:<never-recorded-id>` ref renders as owned=true, because the mirror has no set to check it against -- the exact 'dangling-ref' condition this boolean exists to surface.
recommendation: Add `humanTurnIds = new Set()` to isRefOwnedBySession's options and a mirroring branch before the segment scan (`if (ref.startsWith(HUMAN_TURN_REF_PREFIX)) return humanTurnIds.has(ref.slice(HUMAN_TURN_REF_PREFIX.length));`) plus the bare-id near-miss (`if (humanTurnIds.has(ref)) return false;`), and populate refOwnedOpts.humanTurnIds from `coordinationState.humanTurns.map((r) => r.turnId)` -- the same `accepted-only` posture the existing contributionIds line already takes. Add a test asserting targetRefOwnedBySession===true for a legitimate `human-turn:` disposition ref; the existing 'show renders humanTurns as its own labelled section' test uses a `$ref:produce` targetRef and therefore never touches this path.

summary: replay.mjs does NOT re-check the `attributedTo.id` driver-authored-ref-shape refusal (asgn_ / contribution: / human-turn:), contrary to what the contract doc and CHANGELOG both claim. A hand-crafted log attributing a turn to a driver-authored ref shape replays clean.
evidence: store.mjs:1445 refuses `attributedTo.id` matching /^asgn_/, CONTRIBUTION_REF_PREFIX, or HUMAN_TURN_REF_PREFIX. The replay branch checks only: recordedBy===writerId, attributedTo.id===recordedBy.id, declared-panel-actor, duplicate turnId, externalRef reuse, ordinal contiguity. The ref-shape refusal has no counterpart. Empirically reproduced: a hand-written events.jsonl entry with attributedTo {type:'person', id:'asgn_deadbeefcafe0001'} replays with no error and lands in replayed.humanTurns (printed back as attributedTo.id === 'asgn_deadbeefcafe0001'); same for id 'contribution:x1'. The identical payload IS refused by recordHumanTurn ('validation'), confirming the write door and replay disagree. Doc claim contradicted: coordination-session.md:854-860 heads the list with "**Refusals (write door and replay, independently).**" and includes this refusal in it; the T1 table row (line 885) says "re-checked independently at replay". The T8 row (line 892) enumerates what replay actually re-validates and correctly OMITS this refusal -- so the doc contradicts itself internally. CHANGELOG.md carries the same overclaim.
recommendation: Either add the three-prefix check to the replay branch (four lines, matching store.mjs:1445 exactly), or -- if the omission is deliberate -- fix coordination-session.md:854 and the T1 row and the CHANGELOG line to state plainly that the ref-shape refusal is write-door-only. Preference: add the check; it is the cheap half and T8's whole premise is that replay is an independent gate on a hand-written log.

summary: No `turnId` shape guard at the store door. Unlike contributionId (assertContributionIdShape), a turnId may contain path separators, `..`, or the reserved `human-turn:` prefix -- and because the `human-turn:` branch early-returns before the cross-session segment scan, such a turnId lets a disposition ref claim cross-session reach while the ownership door reports it as owned.
location: src/runner/coordination/store.mjs:1393-1500 (recordHumanTurn, no id-shape check) vs src/runner/coordination/store.mjs:1516-1524 (assertContributionIdShape); early return at store.mjs:1201
evidence: assertContributionIdShape exists specifically because "a path-shaped id reads as session-owned at the ownership doors while its text claims cross-session reach, and a `contribution:`-prefixed id would make `contribution:<id>` ambiguous" (its own doc comment). turnId gets no equivalent. Empirically reproduced: recordHumanTurn accepted turnId '../../../etc/passwd' and turnId 'human-turn:spoof'; with a second session named 'victim' on disk, recordHumanTurn accepted turnId '../victim' and then recordDriverDisposition ACCEPTED targetRef 'human-turn:../victim' (returned targetRef unchanged, replay reconstructed it) -- while the same ref text WITHOUT the namespace prefix ('../victim') is refused. The `human-turn:` branch at store.mjs:1192-1203 returns before reaching the segment scan at store.mjs:1223, so the cross-session guard never runs for any namespaced ref. Mitigating: the request-file boundary applies assertSafeId to step.turnId (verbs/coordination/schema.mjs), and there is a test for it, so this is unreachable via `fgos coordination run` -- it is reachable only from a direct store.mjs API caller. store.mjs is nonetheless described in its own comments as "the pure kernel that is the actual gate a hand-written log passes through", and contributionId got the guard at exactly that layer.
recommendation: Add an assertTurnIdShape mirroring assertContributionIdShape (reject path separators, `..`, and a leading HUMAN_TURN_REF_PREFIX), called from recordHumanTurn before the lock, and re-check it in replay.mjs's human-turn branch. Do NOT instead move the segment scan ahead of the prefix branch -- that would change existing `contribution:` behavior, which is out of this cell's scope.

summary: replay.mjs never validates a recorded turn's own `respondsToRefs` for session ownership, so a hand-crafted log may make a turn respond to a turn that never existed. This is asymmetric with the `human-turn:` disposition-targetRef out-of-order check added a few lines away, and is not disclosed as a gap.
location: src/runner/coordination/replay.mjs:291-300 (respondsToRefs copied verbatim into the record, unchecked) vs src/runner/coordination/replay.mjs:472-488 (disposition targetRef IS checked)
evidence: The replay branch copies event.payload.respondsToRefs straight into the reconstructed record with no ownership or existence check. Empirically reproduced: a hand-written human-turn-recorded event with respondsToRefs ['human-turn:turn_never_existed'] replays with no error, and the reconstructed record carries that ref (show.mjs renderHumanTurn then renders it). The write door DOES check this (store.mjs:1482-1495, via assertDispositionRefOwnedBySession), and replay DOES check the analogous case for a driver-disposition-recorded targetRef in the same namespace (out-of-order-ref, replay.mjs:479). So the omission is specific to this one field. The contract doc's 'Named limitation' paragraph (coordination-session.md:894-908) describes respondsToRefs validation as write-door-only in effect but does not name the replay gap, and the T8 row's list of what replay re-validates omits it silently rather than disclosing it.
recommendation: In the replay human-turn branch, for each respondsToRefs entry starting with HUMAN_TURN_REF_PREFIX, assert the named turn is already in humanTurnIds at that point in the log -- the same out-of-order-ref check and error category the disposition branch already uses. Add a hand-written-log test alongside the existing appendRawHumanTurn cases. If left as-is, disclose it explicitly in the T8 row.

summary: The request door resolves `artifactRef` with path.resolve(ctx.cwd, ...) and applies no workspace-containment check, so a request may attest and existence-probe any file the process can read, including absolute paths and `..` escapes outside the session's repo.
evidence: verbs/coordination/schema.mjs's validateHumanTurnStep deliberately skips assertSafeRefOrId on artifactRef (documented: real relative paths need separators) and checks only non-emptiness. run.mjs then path.resolve's it and readFileSync's it. path.resolve(cwd, '/etc/shadow') === '/etc/shadow'. Consequences are narrow: only a sha256 of the bytes is recorded and returned (no content echo), and ENOENT vs EACCES vs success is distinguishable from the error surface. The recorded artifactRef in the immutable event may therefore point outside the workspace, which weakens the 'revision pins the real bytes the transcription rests on' story for any later verifier that assumes a repo-relative path. Mitigating and explicitly relied upon by the module: the request file is operator-authored trusted data (this module's own header doctrine), so this is a robustness/provenance-clarity issue, not an untrusted-input trust-boundary break.
recommendation: Optional. If tightened, reject an absolute artifactRef and any resolved path outside ctx.repoRoot at the request boundary, and say so in the Human Turn Provenance section. If left as-is, add one sentence to the contract doc noting artifactRef is workspace-relative by convention only.

summary: Test-quality gap, not a code defect on its own: three refusal/mirror behaviors have no test, and the one existing `show` test is constructed so it cannot catch R-P03.1-01.
evidence: (a) The 'show renders humanTurns as its own labelled section' test creates its disposition with targetRef '$ref:produce' and evidenceRefs [], so no human-turn ref ever reaches isRefOwnedBySession -- had it used a `human-turn:` targetRef and asserted targetRefOwnedBySession===true, R-P03.1-01 would have failed the suite. (b) No replay test covers the attributedTo ref-shape refusal (there is none to test -- see R-P03.1-02). (c) No replay test covers respondsToRefs at all (see R-P03.1-04). Positive counterweight, checked deliberately: I looked for a phantom test that would still pass with its refusal removed and did not find one. The six store-door refusals each have a dedicated test whose assertion is specific (error class + category and/or a message regex), the replay tests use hand-written events.jsonl entries via appendRawHumanTurn rather than events that already passed the write door, and the revision test independently recomputes the expected sha256 from the file rather than echoing the reported value.
recommendation: Extend the existing show test to use a `human-turn:` targetRef and assert ownership===true (this is the regression test for R-P03.1-01), and add the two replay cases named above alongside whichever of R-P03.1-02/04 are fixed.
